title: Implement rate-adaptive trace sampler and span coalescing to cut per-request overhead
creator: Ava Collins
description: Problem: Our end-to-end request CPU and p95 latency has regressed on high-QPS services due to tracing overhead. In particular, creating and serializing hundreds of short-lived spans for hot paths (auth checks, header parsing, middleware) dominates per-request allocations when tracing is enabled. Objective: reduce end-to-end overhead of tracing without losing signal for errors and tail latency. Proposed solution: 1) Rate-adaptive sampler that adjusts per-service/per-route sampling probability using a sliding-window estimator of emitted-traces-per-minute and observed error-rate; 2) Span coalescing: collapse low-information spans in hot paths into a single aggregated span with counters, avoiding object churn; 3) Fast path optimizations: avoid allocations when trace is sampled=false, inline decision path, and use a lock-free reservoir for tail-sampled spans; 4) Controlled rollout via feature flag and canary metrics (trace emission, CPU, p95 latency). This ticket covers design, implementation in the tracing library, unit + integration tests, benchmarking harness changes, and a phased rollout plan with dashboards and alert thresholds.
acceptance_criteria: end-to-end p95 on the canary service improves by at least 8% compared to the current traced version when trace sampling is enabled
emitted traces per minute per service is reduced by at least 60% for high-QPS routes without increasing error trace capture rate by more than 5%
span coalescing reduces average number of spans per sampled trace by >= 40% for instrumented hot paths
new sampler exposes metrics: sampler.adjustments, sampler.current_rate_{service}, sampler.emitted_traces, sampler.tail_reservoir_size
feature is gated behind runtime feature flag and tested on two canary clusters before org-wide rollout
unit and integration tests for sampler logic and coalescer added with >=90% branch coverage for new modules
updates: 2026-03-06: Kickoff design sync with tracing, runtime, and platform telemetry. Decided on sliding-window estimator (60s window) and per-route bucketing by route hash.

2026-03-08: Prototype of span coalescer implemented in tracing-lib: coalescer merges contiguous low-duration spans under a single parent and emits counters. Initial microbench shows 25% allocation reduction.
2026-03-10: Benchmark harness updated to run 100k reqs/min with realistic middleware. Early results: rate-adaptive sampler reduces emitted traces by ~52% at default policy; p95 improved by 6%.
2026-03-12: Design review with PM/RE (Sophie Tan) and runtime owners. Feedback: add per-service guard rails and ensure KMS keys for trace payloads unaffected. Added guardrail metric and rollout plan.
2026-03-13: Opened PR #3784 implementing lock-free reservoir and zero-alloc decision hot path. Requesting review from @ryan and @mei
2026-03-14: Canary rollout plan drafted and dashboards annotated. Preparing synthetic canary run tomorrow with feature flag enabled on two staging clusters.
notes: Trade-offs: aggressive sampling reduces signal for rare failure modes; mitigated by maintaining tail reservoir and error-weighted upsampling. Span coalescing hides span-level timing detail — keep it opt-in per-instrumentation and preserve counters/annotations for downstream analytics. Monitoring: we will create derived dashboards for errors-per-sampled-trace, sampling-rate-by-route, and sampler.adjustment-events. Alert if emitted_traces_per_minute deviates from target by >25% or if error capture rate for top-10 routes drops by >10%. Rollout: canary -> 2 regions -> org-wide with kill-switch on feature flag.
